SMTO-SKL-0039 — SMTO couldn't find that shared drive

GUID: 36254543-a436-5e04-b8ba-1f06d97873a0
Slug: google-drive-drive-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • Google Drive says the shared drive doesn't exist for the account SMTO used. It may have been deleted or renamed away, or this account may not be a member.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Google Drive in your browser with the same account and look under Shared drives for the one you meant. If it's missing there too, the account isn't a member or the shared drive was removed.
  2. Ask SMTO to list the shared drives it can see, and choose the right one from that list. Picking from the list gives SMTO the exact shared drive instead of an old or mistyped one.
  3. If the shared drive belongs to your team but isn't listed, ask its manager to add your Google account as a member. Only members can see a shared drive and its files.

What success looks like

  • SMTO lists the shared drive and can show its files.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't switch to a different shared drive with a similar name without checking.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Drive returned HTTP 404 or 410 for a request scoped to the supplied shared drive (drive_id) under the selected account.

What this means

  • Google returns HTTP 404 or 410 for a shared-drive-scoped request. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns HTTP 404 or 410 for a shared-drive-scoped request.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify drive_id and current membership without guessing another drive.

How to fix it

  • provider_error mapped a 404/410 on a drive-scoped request to drive_not_found. Verify the exact drive_id (google_drive.drives lists shared drives visible to the account) and that the selected account_ref is a member of that shared drive.
  • Verify the exact drive_id and account membership.

Retry and execution caution

  • Verify the exact drive_id and account membership.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended shared drive is visible to the authorized account.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
